text:
andrew: Heads-up question — ran into weirdness with the Java client auth. If I initialize the client with a service account key that omits the `project_id` field, requests still show a project in logs. Is the SDK implicitly falling back to GCE/GKE metadata or ADC?

nina: short answer: yes, it can. If ADC finds a project in the environment (GCE metadata, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, or gcloud config), the token exchange layer may include that as the inferred project in some request headers.

andrew: ok — wanted to confirm behavior for streaming: do we cache that inferred project on the client instance? i'm worried about multi-tenant hosts where the env var changes between processes.

ashley: the Java SDK keeps the inferred project as part of the Credentials object once constructed. So if you create a long-lived client while env vars change, you won't pick up the new project until you recreate credentials.

kevin: to add: the service-account JWT itself doesn't need project_id to be valid, but downstream routing + audit logs sometimes prefer an explicit project. That's why SDKs try to surface an inferred one.

andrew: got it — is there a recommended pattern to avoid surprises when running in pooled containers? i.e., refresh creds per-request or reinit client on task lease?

nina: recommendations: 1) avoid mutating GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT at runtime; 2) if you must change per-job, create short-lived clients per job or call `CredentialsProvider#refresh` (Java) after env swap; 3) for streaming connections, prefer per-tenant routing so you don't reuse a single socket across tenants.

andrew: thanks. can you share the minimal code snippet to reinit creds without rebuilding the whole client?

ashley: sure. in Java you can do:
```java
// recreate credentials and inject into client builder
GoogleCredentials creds = GoogleCredentials.fromStream(new FileInputStream("/path/to/key.json"));
creds = creds.createScoped(Arrays.asList("https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"));
MyServiceClient client = MyServiceClient.newBuilder()
    .setCredentialsProvider(FixedCredentialsProvider.create(creds))
    .build();
```

ashley: if you want to hot-swap on the same process, close the old client and build a new one per job. It's cheap relative to per-token overhead.

kevin: also note token caching: the lower-level library caches access tokens until expiry. If you swap creds but keep the old token cached, you'll need to force a refresh (call `creds.refresh()` or clear the cache by recreating the creds object).

andrew: perfect. last q: any gotchas for our internal streaming layer where we do reauth on 401s? will inferred-project differ on reauth path vs initial auth?

nina: reauth path uses the same Credentials object, so inferred project stays consistent. But if you rebuild creds logic during reauth to use ADC again, it may pick up a different project. So keep reauth deterministic.

devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/devex/auth-project-inference — has migration tips and a small checklist for container pools. :books: 

andrew: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
